name: TDC ADMET Clearance_Microsome_AZ
description: Predict the intrinsic clearance of a compound measured in liver microsomes, the rate at which liver enzymes remove it (mL per minute per gram) from its molecular structure, given as a SMILES string (endpoint Clearance_Microsome_AZ of the Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET benchmark group). The measured compounds are split by molecular scaffold into a training, a validation and a test part. The test part is fixed; the candidate is run five times (seeds 1 to 5), each time with a different division of the other compounds into training and validation. It receives the training and validation compounds with their values and the test compounds without, and returns one prediction per test compound. Each of the five runs is a separate process that receives only these arguments: it cannot read the evaluator's files, start other processes or open network connections, and it has 700 seconds. The score is the Spearman rank correlation between the predictions and the measured values of the test compounds, averaged over the five runs; higher is better, and only the order of the predictions counts.

sources.locator: Mechanistic insights from comparing intrinsic clearance values between human liver microsomes and hepatocytes to guide drug design
Clearance, AstraZeneca: regression, 1,102 drugs for microsomes; references the AstraZeneca ChEMBL deposit and Di et al. 2012.

Huang et al. (2022), Artificial intelligence foundation for therapeutic science (Nat Chem Biol): the Therapeutics Data Commons paper linked from the TDC site, benchmark paper only; also arXiv 2102.09548, Therapeutics Data Commons: Machine Learning Datasets and Tasks for Drug Discovery and Development.

requirements.datasets: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_smiles, train_y, valid_smiles, valid_y, test_smiles, info) -> sequence of finite numbers, one per test molecule in the given order: the predicted value. train_smiles, valid_smiles and test_smiles are lists of SMILES strings, train_y and valid_y lists of numbers; info has name, metric, kind ('regression' or 'binary') and seed. Score: mean over the seeds 1 to 5 of the Spearman rank correlation between predictions and measured values on the test part, maximized.
notes: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet

limitations: Leaders are large tuned ensembles or foundation-model fine-tunes.
Needs PyTDC and rdkit: not in .venv-tasks, so the evaluator restarts itself under tools/venv-admet (created by the README's setup steps).

Every scoring call of the candidate runs in the main suite's sandbox (a child process with an audit hook, 700 s and 6 GB for one call): it keeps a search from coming across the test labels and is not a security boundary against a candidate written to attack the evaluator.
One evaluation of the starting program took 210 s in the run of 2026-11-11, more than the arena's default limit of 120 s: raise AR_EVAL_TIMEOUT for this task.
The record was found in a hashed snapshot of its source; it is not replayed. See VALIDITY.md.

checks: leaderboard rank 1 (Spearman): MapLight + GNN Jim Notwell 0.63
notes: leaderboard page is a live snapshot, undated

science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
science_relevance.reason: The cited paper(s) have the prediction or measurement of this property as their main objective; the task scores a structure-based predictor of the same property.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the in vitro intrinsic clearance of a compound measured in liver microsomes from its structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Microsomal intrinsic clearance is the high-throughput early measure of oxidative metabolic stability and is used to predict hepatic clearance and dose.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights from comparing intrinsic clearance values between human liver microsomes and hepatocytes to guide drug design
papers.task_relation: The task predicts in vitro intrinsic clearance from structure for one of the two systems; the cited paper explains how the two measurements relate (TDC cites it for separating them) and does not build the predictor.
papers.primary_goal: Compare intrinsic clearance measured in human liver microsomes and in hepatocytes to explain their differences and guide drug design.
